chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who has his wife with him on a journey and cannot find water; can he sleep with his wife? He (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not like him to do so, except if he fears upon himself.'

I said: 'Does he seek pleasure thereby, or is he craving for women?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The craving is [considered] fearing upon himself.' I said: 'He seeks pleasure thereby?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is permissible.'

I said: 'For it is reported from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that Abu Dharr (may Allah have mercy on him) asked him about this, so he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Go to your wife, you will be rewarded.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Do I go to them and get rewarded?' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Just as when you go to the forbidden, you are burdened [with sin], so similarly, when you go to the permissible, you will be rewarded.'
So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not see that he, when he fears upon himself, so he goes to the permissible, would be rewarded?'
ai.seo_question: Can a man sleep with his wife during travel if he cannot find water for ablution?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the principle of *al-shabiq* (sexual desire) as a valid excuse for neglecting ablution during travel, reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing spiritual rigor with natural human instincts. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the permissibility of marital intimacy in this state, countering ascetic tendencies by linking the reward for fulfilling natural desires to the burden of avoiding prohibitions, as cited from the Prophet’s dialogue with Abu Dharr. This underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that *halal* acts, when performed with proper intention, carry spiritual merit comparable to *haram* acts in terms of accountability.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who happens to have his wife with him in the journey. He cannot find the water, can he sleep with his wife?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not like it if he were to do so, except if he fears upon himsef’.

I said, ‘He seeks the pleasure with that or he happens to have craving for the women?’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The craving is his fear upon himself’. I said, ‘He seeks the pleasure with that?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is Permissible’.

I said, ‘But is has been reported from the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> that Abu Zarr<sup>as</sup> asked him<sup>saww</sup> about this, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Go to you wife, you will be Rewarded’. So he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! I<sup>as</sup> go to them and I<sup>as</sup> get Rewarded (for it)?’ So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Just as when you<sup>as</sup> go to the Prohibition, you<sup>as</sup> are burdened, so similar to that, when you go to the Permissible, you will be Rewarded’.
So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do you not see that he, when he fears upon himself, so he goes to the Permissible, would be Rewarded?’
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who is on a journey with his wife and they cannot find water; if he can go to bed with his wife. He (the Imam) said, ‘I do not like it unless he is afraid for himself.’

I then asked, ‘Is it about the case of seeking to satisfy one’s lust or is about the case of pressing desire for women?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Pressing desire for women of one’s fear for one’s self.’ I then asked, ‘Can one seek thereby pleasure?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is lawful.’

I then asked, ‘It is narrated from the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, that once abu Dharr, may Allah grant him mercy, asked him about it and he (the Messenger of Allah) said, “You can go to your wife; you will be rewarded.” He asked, “O Messenger of Allah, I go to my wife and receive reward?” The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, said, “It is like when you commit an unlawful act; you have sinned, so also is the case of your doing a lawful act; you receive rewards.’”
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Consider when one fears his soul, then performs a lawful act; he then is rewarded.’”
